title: Verified by Construction: Machine-Checked Proofs for Hand-Written Transformer Circuits and Their Composition
editor_models: none (author-written circuits; verifies agent-written snapshots from Singh's WSP study, agent model not stated)

target_networks.name: hand-written algorithmic transformers from Singh's WSP study (parity, boolean circuit, digit counting, word reversal, sort, linear interpolation, addition, multiplication)
OPT-1.3B / 2.7B / 6.7B hosts with grafted refusal circuit
GPT-2 small (naive vs compensated graft check)

domain: formal verification / AI safety (refusal circuits, key gating, watermarks)
tasks_benchmarks: Lean 4 proofs over full task input spaces (up to about 5.4e12 prompts)
deployment transforms (fp16, bf16, TF32, int8, int4, pruning)

headline_result.text: Seven agent-written weight-space programs (up to 1.3M parameters) were proved correct on every input, one multiplication snapshot with 100% sampled accuracy was refuted by the counterexample 89984*48898=, and a proved refusal circuit grafted into OPT-6.7B fired on 2480 of 2480 trigger positions.

notes_for_review: Directly relevant as an audit of agent-written weights: it formally verifies the hand-written transformers from Singh's companion WSP study and shows one snapshot that passed the study's 200-sample evaluation is wrong. The second half (grafting safety circuits into OPT hosts with Lean proofs) is a method contribution where the author, not an LLM, writes the circuits. Evidence is strong in the formal sense (kernel-checked proofs over whole input domains), but the link from Lean constants to deployed tensors rests on an unverified exporter, and floating-point execution is only measured.
